title: Temurah 30
description: The Gemara settles whose view the baraita on a widow’s payment follows and why the maidservant and the slave count as a prostitute’s payment, then the mishna defines the price of a dog, rules on money, wine and birds given as payment and on the offspring of forbidden animals, and the Gemara debates when Rabbi Eliezer forbids those offspring.
topics: 📜 Rabbi Elazar’s view of an unmarried couple, and why the baraita names a widow and a High Priest
🔗 “Lie with my slave”: Rav Huna’s euphemism and Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak’s Hebrew slave
🐕 The price of a dog: a lamb in place of a dog, and partners who divide ten lambs against nine and a dog
✌️ “Both of them”: two and not four, and “them” and not their offspring
🐂 Offspring of forbidden animals, and the excrement of a stoned ox and of calves of idolatry
🍷 Money, wine, wheat that became flour, consecrated items and birds given as payment
🏛️ “The House of the Lord”: the red heifer, gold plates and registering a prostitute on a Paschal offering
⚖️ Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis on offspring: Rav Naḥman and Rava in two versions

a1.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הִיא, דְּאָמַר: פָּנוּי הַבָּא עַל הַפְּנוּיָה שֶׁלֹּא לְשׁוּם אִישׁוּת עֲשָׂאָהּ זוֹנָה. אִי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, מַאי אִירְיָא אַלְמָנָה? נִיתְנֵי פְּנוּיָה!

a2.he: אַלְמָנָה אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וּבִנְיַן אָב הוּא — לָא נִיתַּסְרוּ, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.

a3.he: הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ ״הֵא לָךְ טָלֶה זֶה״ כּוּ׳. וְהָא שִׁפְחָה לְעֶבֶד מִישְׁרָא שַׁרְיָא! אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: אֶצְלוֹ קָאָמַר, וְהָא דְּקָתָנֵי ״עֶבֶד״ — לִישָּׁנָא מְעַלְּיָא קָאָמַר.

a4.he: אִי הָכִי, מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי? אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק: לְעוֹלָם עַבְדִּי, וְכִי קָתָנֵי בְּעֶבֶד עִבְרִי.

a5.he: אִי הָכִי, מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּנַן? שִׁפְחָה לְעֶבֶד עִבְרִי מִישְׁרָא שַׁרְיָא! הָכָא בְמַאי עָסְקִינַן — כְּגוֹן דְּלֵית לֵיהּ אִשָּׁה וּבָנִים, דְּתַנְיָא: אֵין לוֹ אִשָּׁה וּבָנִים — אֵין רַבּוֹ מוֹסֵר לוֹ שִׁפְחָה כְּנַעֲנִית, יֵשׁ לוֹ אִשָּׁה וּבָנִים — רַבּוֹ מוֹסֵר לוֹ שִׁפְחָה כְּנַעֲנִית.

a6.he: מַתְנִי׳ וְאֵיזֶהוּ ״מְחִיר כֶּלֶב״? הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ ״הֵולָיךְ טָלֶה זֶה תַּחַת כֶּלֶב״.

a7.he: וְכֵן שְׁנֵי שׁוּתָּפִין שֶׁחָלְקוּ, אֶחָד נָטַל עֲשָׂרָה וְאֶחָד תִּשְׁעָה וָכֶלֶב, שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד הַכֶּלֶב אָסוּר, וְשֶׁעִם הַכֶּלֶב מוּתָּר.

a8.he: אֶתְנַן הַכֶּלֶב וּמְחִיר זוֹנָה — הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מוּתָּרִין, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״שְׁנַיִם״ וְלֹא אַרְבָּעָה. וַלְדוֹתֵיהֶן מוּתָּרִין — ״הֵן״ וְלֹא וַלְדוֹתֵיהֶן.

a9.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״מְחִיר כֶּלֶב״ — זֶהוּ חֲלִיפֵי כֶלֶב, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״תִּמְכֹּר עַמְּךָ בְלֹא הוֹן וְלֹא רִבִּיתָ בִּמְחִירֵיהֶם״.

a10.he: אֵימָא אֶתְנַן (זונה) [מַמָּשׁ], אִם כֵּן (לא קרב) הָווּ תְּלָתָא, ״גַּם שְׁנֵיהֶם״ — וְלֹא שְׁלֹשָׁה!

a11.he: מִי קָאָמְרִינַן אֲנַן אֶתְנַן וּמְחִיר? אֶתְנַן וְלֹא מְחִיר קָאָמְרִינַן.

a12.he: אִם כֵּן, נֵימָא קְרָא ״לֹא תָבִיא אֶתְנַן זוֹנָה וָכֶלֶב״, מִדִּכְתִיב ״אֶתְנַן זוֹנָה וּמְחִיר כֶּלֶב״ — שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.

a13.he: הַשּׁוּתָּפִין שֶׁחָלְקוּ, אֶחָד נָטַל כּוּ׳. [אַמַּאי]? נִיפּוֹק חַדא לַהֲדֵי כַּלְבָּא, וְהָנָךְ כּוּלְּהוּ לִישְׁתְּרוֹ! הָכָא בְמַאי עָסְקִינַן? כְּגוֹן דִּטְפֵי דְּמֵי כֶלֶב מֵחַד מִינַּיְיהוּ, (והאי) [וְהָהוּא] טוּפְיָינָא דְּכֶלֶב שְׁדֵי בְּכוּלְּהוּ.

a14.he: אֶתְנַן כֶּלֶב וּמְחִיר זוֹנָה מוּתָּר כּוּ׳. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִפַּרְזַקְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:

b1.he: מְנַָא הָא מִילְּתָא דַאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן אֵין זְנוּת לִבְהֵמוֹת? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא (נִישְׁמוֹט) [לִישְׁתְּמִיט] קְרָא לִכְתּוֹב ״אֶתְנַן זוֹנָה וָכֶלֶב״.

b2.he: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: מִנַּיִן לְאֶתְנַן כֶּלֶב וּמְחִיר זוֹנָה שֶׁמּוּתָּרִין? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״שְׁנַיִם״ וְלֹא אַרְבָּעָה. וַלְדוֹתֵיהֶן מוּתָּרִין, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״גַּם שְׁנֵיהֶם״ — ״הֵם״ וְלֹא וַלְדוֹתֵיהֶן.

b3.he: אָמַר רָבָא: וְלַד הַנִּרְבַּעַת אֲסוּרָה, הִיא וּוְלָדָהּ נִרְבְּעוּ. נוֹגַחַת אֲסוּרָה, הִיא וּוְלָדָהּ נָגְחוּ.

b4.he: וְלַד מוּקְצֶה וְנֶעֱבָד — מוּתָּר. מַאי טַעְמָא? לְאִימֵּיהּ אַקְצְיַהּ, לְאִימֵּיהּ פָּלְחִי לַהּ. אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: וְלַד מוּקְצֶה וְנֶעֱבָד — אָסוּר. מַאי טַעְמָא? דְּנִיחָא לֵיהּ בְּנִיפְחֵיהּ.

b5.he: אָמַר רַב אַחָדְבוּי בַּר אַמֵּי, אָמַר רַב: הַמְקַדֵּשׁ בְּפֶרֶשׁ שׁוֹר הַנִּסְקָל, מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת. בְּפֶרֶשׁ עֶגְלֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, אֵינָהּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת. מַאי טַעְמָא? אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא קְרָא, וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא סְבָרָא.

b6.he: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא סְבָרָא: נִיחָא לֵיהּ גַּבֵּי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּנִיפְחֵיהּ, גַּבֵּי שׁוֹר הַנִּסְקָל — לָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ בְּנִיפְחֵיהּ.

b7.he: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא קְרָא, גַּבֵּי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כְּתִיב: ״וְהָיִיתָ חֵרֶם כָּמוֹהוּ״, כֹּל שֶׁאַתָּה מְהַיֶּה מִמֶּנּוּ הֲרֵי הוּא כָּמוֹהוּ. גַּבֵּי שׁוֹר הַנִּסְקָל כְּתִיב: ״לֹא יֵאָכֵל אֶת בְּשָׂרוֹ״ — בְּשָׂרוֹ אָסוּר, פִּרְשׁוֹ מוּתָּר.

b8.he: מַתְנִי׳ נָתַן לָהּ מָעוֹת — הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מוּתָּרִין. יֵינוֹת וּשְׁמָנִים וּסְלָתוֹת, וְכׇל דָּבָר שֶׁכַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ קָרֵב עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ — אָסוּר. נָתַן לָהּ מוּקְדָּשִׁין — הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מוּתָּרִין.

b9.he: עוֹפוֹת — הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ אֲסוּרִין, שֶׁהָיָה בַּדִּין: מָה אִם הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין, שֶׁהַמּוּם פּוֹסֵל בָּהֶן — אֵין אֶתְנַן וּמְחִיר חָל עֲלֵיהֶן; עוֹף, שֶׁאֵין הַמּוּם פּוֹסֵל בּוֹ — אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא אֶתְנַן וּמְחִיר חָל עָלָיו? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״לְכׇל נֶדֶר״ — לְהָבִיא אֶת הָעוֹף.

b10.he: כׇּל הָאֲסוּרִין לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ — וַלְדוֹתֵיהֶן מוּתָּרִין. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: וְלַד טְרֵפָה לֹא יִקְרַב עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ. רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אוֹמֵר: כְּשֵׁירָה שֶׁיָּנְקָה מִן הַטְּרֵפָה — פְּסוּלָה מֵעַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ. כׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ טְרֵפָה — אֵין פּוֹדִין אוֹתָן, שֶׁאֵין פּוֹדִין אֶת הַקֳּדָשִׁים לְהַאֲכִילָן לִכְלָבִים.

b11.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נָתַן לָהּ חִיטִּין וַעֲשָׂאָתַן סוֹלֶת, זֵיתִים וַעֲשָׂאָתַן שֶׁמֶן, עֲנָבִים וַעֲשָׂאָתַן יַיִן. תָּנֵי חֲדָא: אֲסוּרִים, וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: מוּתָּרִין. אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: תָּנֵי גּוּרְיוֹן דְּמִן אַסְפּוֹרַק — בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹסְרִין וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין.

b12.he: בֵּית הִלֵּל סָבְרִי: ״הֵם״ — וְלֹא וַלְדוֹתֵיהֶן, ״הֵם״ — וְלֹא שִׁינּוּיֵיהֶן.

b13.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי סָבְרִי: ״הֵם״ — וְלֹא וַלְדוֹתֵיהֶן, ״גַּם״ — לְרַבּוֹת שִׁינּוּיֵיהֶן, וּלְבֵית הִלֵּל, הָכְתִיב ״גַּם״! ״גַּם״ לְבֵית הִלֵּל קַשְׁיָא.

b14.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״בֵּית ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ״ — פְּרָט לְפָרָה, שֶׁאֵין בָּאָה לַבַּיִת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: לְרַבּוֹת אֶת הָרִיקּוּעִין.

b15.he: מַאן חֲכָמִים? אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא: נָתַן לָהּ זָהָב, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵין עוֹשִׂין רִיקּוּעִין, אֲפִילּוּ אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּית הַכַּפּוֹרֶת.

b16.he: נָתַן לָהּ מוּקְדָּשִׁין — הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ מוּתָּרִין כּוּ׳.

b17.he: וְיִהְיוּ מוּקְדָּשִׁין אֶתְנַן וּמְחִיר חָל עֲלֵיהֶן, מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר: וּמָה עוֹפוֹת שֶׁאֵין הַמּוּם פּוֹסֵל בָּהֶן — אֶתְנַן וּמְחִיר חָל עֲלֵיהֶן, מוּקְדָּשִׁים שֶׁהַמּוּם פּוֹסֵל בָּהֶן — אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁאֶתְנַן וּמְחִיר חָל עֲלֵיהֶן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״לְכׇל נֶדֶר״ — לְהוֹצִיא אֶת הַנָּדוּר.

b18.he: טַעְמָא דְּמַעֲטִינְהוּ קְרָא, הָא לָא מַעֲטִינְהוּ קְרָא הֲוָה אֲמִינָא: כִּי יָהֵיב לַהּ מוּקְדָּשִׁין — חָל עֲלֵיהֶן אֶתְנַן וּמְחִיר? וְהָא לָאו מָמוֹנָא הוּא!

b19.he: אָמַר רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא: בְּמַמְנֶה עַל פִּסְחוֹ, וְרַבִּי הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא: ״וְאִם יִמְעַט הַבַּיִת מִהְיוֹת מִשֶּׂה״.

b20.he: הַחֲיֵיהוּ מִשֶּׂה, מִכְּדֵי אֲכִילָה וְלֹא מִכְּדֵי מִקָּח.

b21.he: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אַף מִכְּדֵי מִקָּח, שֶׁאִם אֵין לוֹ מַמְנֶה אֲחֵרִים עִמּוֹ עַל פִּסְחוֹ וְעַל חֲגִיגָתוֹ, וּמְעוֹתָיו חוּלִּין, שֶׁעַל מְנָת כֵּן הִקְדִּישׁוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל פִּסְחֵיהֶן.

b22.he: כָּל הָאֲסוּרִים לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַב: כָּל הָאֲסוּרִים לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ וַלְדוֹתֵיהֶן מוּתָּרִים, וְתָנֵי עֲלַהּ: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹסֵר.

b23.he: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מַחְלוֹקֶת שֶׁעִיבְּרוּ וּלְבַסּוֹף נִרְבְּעוּ, דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר ״עוּבָּר יֶרֶךְ אִמּוֹ הוּא״, וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי ״לָאו יֶרֶךְ אִמּוֹ הוּא״, אֲבָל נִרְבְּעוּ וּלְבַסּוֹף עִיבְּרוּ — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מוּתָּרִין.

b24.he: רָבָא אָמַר: מַחְלוֹקֶת שֶׁנִּרְבְּעוּ וּלְבַסּוֹף עִיבְּרוּ, דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם אָסוּר, וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם מוּתָּר.

b25.he: אֲבָל עִיבְּרוּ וּלְבַסּוֹף נִרְבְּעוּ — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֲסוּרִין. וְרָבָא לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר רָבָא: וְלַד נִרְבַּעַת אָסוּר, הִיא וּוְלָדָהּ נִרְבְּעוּ, וְלַד נוֹגַחַת אָסוּר, הִיא וּוְלָדָהּ נָגְחוּ.

b26.he: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא אָמְרִי לַהּ. אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מַחְלוֹקֶת שֶׁנִּרְבְּעוּ כְּשֶׁהֵן מוּקְדָּשִׁין, דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר בִּיזּוּי מִילְּתָא, וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי לָא. אֲבָל נִרְבְּעוּ כְּשֶׁהֵן חוּלִּין, הוֹאִיל וְהִשְׁתַּנּוּ — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל מוּתָּרִין.

b27.he: רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מַחְלוֹקֶת כְּשֶׁנִּרְבְּעוּ כְּשֶׁהֵן חוּלִּין, דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סָבַר: בִּיזּוּי מִילְּתָא, וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: הוֹאִיל וְהִשְׁתַּנּוּ — מוּתָּרִין, אֲבָל נִרְבְּעוּ כְּשֶׁהֵן מוּקְדָּשִׁין — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֲסוּרִין.

messages.text: Continued from 29b: a baraita forbids the payment of a widow to a High Priest, or of a divorcée or a ḥalutza to an ordinary priest, although betrothal takes effect with them. The Gemara asked whose opinion that baraita follows.
Gemara
It is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Elazar, who says:
With regard to an unmarried man who engaged in intercourse with an unmarried woman not for the purpose of marriage, he has thereby caused her to become a prostitute.

notes.dh: ר' אלעזר היא דאמר פנוי הבא כו'
notes.he: בעילת זנות קרי זונה הלכך אתנן נמי אסור דאתנן זונה קרינא ביה ואנא דאמרי כרבנן:
notes.en: It is Rabbi Elazar, who says: an unmarried man who has intercourse etc.: he calls [a woman who had] intercourse of promiscuity a “prostitute.” Therefore her payment is also forbidden, since the term “payment of a prostitute” applies to it. And I [Abaye], who said [that the payment of a Jewish prostitute is permitted], hold like the Rabbis.

notes.he: ואתננה אסור אע"ג דתפסי בה קידושין:
notes.en: He has made her a prostitute: and her payment is forbidden, even though betrothal takes effect with her.

messages.text: It is for this reason that her payment is prohibited to be sacrificed on the altar. By contrast, Abaye holds in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, who disagree with Rabbi Elazar.

If the baraita is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Elazar, why mention specifically the prohibition of a widow who is paid for engaging in intercourse with a High Priest? Let it teach that payment is prohibited even in the case of an unmarried man who engaged in intercourse with an unmarried woman.

notes.he: מאי איריא דתני כגון אלמנה לכהן גדול ליתני כגון פנויה (דהא) [דוודאי] תפסי בה קידושי ואמאי קאמר כגון אלמנה:
notes.en: If it is Rabbi Elazar: why specifically teach “for example, a widow to a High Priest”? Let it teach “for example, an unmarried woman,” with whom betrothal certainly takes effect. Why does it say “for example, a widow”?

messages.text: It was necessary for the tanna to cite the example of a widow who is paid for engaging in intercourse with a High Priest, as it might enter your mind to say: Since the case of an unmarried man who engaged in intercourse with an unmarried woman, which is not a forbidden relationship by Torah law, is the paradigm example of prohibited payment to a prostitute, perhaps in a situation where the relationship is forbidden by Torah law, the payment should not be prohibited.

notes.he: אי נקט פנויה ה"א פנויה אין דליכא איסורא אבל כל אתנן של אשה האסורה לו לא ניתסר דהא כתיב בקרא זונה וסתם זונה היינו בפנוי ופנויה לר' אלעזר:
notes.en: It is the paradigm: had it stated an unmarried woman, I would have said: an unmarried woman, yes [her payment is forbidden], since there is no prohibition involved; but the payment of any woman who is forbidden to him should not be forbidden, since the verse writes “prostitute,” and the ordinary prostitute is [the case of] an unmarried man with an unmarried woman, according to Rabbi Elazar.

notes.he: ללמד שאין אתנן אסור אלא בפנוי ופנויה אבל מאלמנה דאסירא ליה לכ"ג לא קמ"ל. ל"א הא מני דקתני אלמנה לכ"ג אתננה אסור ר"ע היא דאמר בפ' החולץ אין קדושין תופסין בחייבי לאוין הלכך כעריות דכריתות דמיין ולרבא דאמר כל זונה הוי אתנן מאי שנא דקתני כגון אלמנה אפי' פנויה נמי דהא רבא לא דריש להאי תועבה כאביי אף זונה נמי לא מיתסר עד דאמר לה בהדיא הילך אתנן אבל בסתמא מתנה בעלמא הוא דלא הויא זונה בחדא בעילה בסתמא ודלא כר"א אבל היכא דזונה מעיקרא היא לרבא נמי בסתמא אתנן הוא ואפילו פנויה:
notes.en:
And it is the paradigm: [one might think it comes] to teach that payment is forbidden only with an unmarried man and an unmarried woman, but not with a widow, who is forbidden to a High Priest; it teaches us [otherwise].
Another version: whose view is this, which teaches that the payment of a widow to a High Priest is forbidden? It is Rabbi Akiva, who says in chapter HaḤoletz [Yevamot] that betrothal does not take effect with those liable for negative prohibitions; therefore they are like the forbidden relations punishable by karet.
And according to Rava, who says that [the payment of] every prostitute is payment, why does it teach specifically “for example, a widow”? [It should teach] even an unmarried woman, since Rava does not expound this word “abomination” as Abaye does. [The answer is that, like a widow,] a prostitute too is not forbidden until he says to her explicitly, “Here is payment for you”; but without specifying, it is a mere gift, since she does not become a prostitute through one act of intercourse without specification. This is unlike Rabbi Elazar. But where she was a prostitute from the outset, according to Rava too it is payment even without specification, even [if she is] unmarried.

notes.he: אלמנה איצטריך ליה למימר דסד"א הואיל ובנין אב הוא הא דר' אלעזר דקאמר עשאה זונה (דומיא) [וטמא] דכולהו ילפי מהכא מה פנויה שאין בה טומאה איסור אחר ולא איסור לאו שבא עליה (שלא) [אלא] לשום אישות ותפסי בה קידושי אתננה אסור אף כל דומ' דפנויה דלית בה איסור לאו ותפסי בה קדושין אתננה אסור אבל אלמנה וגרושה אע"ג דתפסי בהו קידושין כיון דאית בהו איסור לאו אימא לא ליתסר אתננהו קמ"ל. דלהכי איצטריך ליה למיתני כגון אלמנה וכו' דאסירי:
notes.en: It needed to state a widow: for it might enter your mind to say that, since it is the paradigm, this [ruling] of Rabbi Elazar, who says “he has made her a prostitute,” I would have said that all are derived from here: just as an unmarried woman, with whom there is no prohibition of impurity and no negative prohibition, but only that he had intercourse with her not for the sake of marriage, and with whom betrothal takes effect, her payment is forbidden, so too anyone similar to an unmarried woman, with no negative prohibition and with whom betrothal takes effect, her payment is forbidden. But a widow and a divorcée, even though betrothal takes effect with them, since there is a negative prohibition with them, I might say their payment is not forbidden. It teaches us [otherwise]. That is why it needed to teach “for example, a widow etc.,” [whose payments] are forbidden. [The printed text here is corrupt; we follow the editors’ corrections.]

messages.text: Therefore, the baraita teaches us that payment to a prostitute is prohibited to be sacrificed on the altar even when the relationship is forbidden by Torah law, as in the case of a widow who is paid for engaging in intercourse with a High Priest.

notes.he: ל"א אמר לך אביי הא סיפא ר' עקיבא היא דאמר אין קדושין תופסין בחייבי לאוין וקאמר דכל זונה דלא תפסי בה קידושי היינו עריות ועובדת כוכבים דומיא דאלמנה לכ"ג דלא תפסי בה קידושי אתננה אסור אבל זונה ישראלית דתפסי בה קידושי אתננה מותר:
notes.en: Another version: Abaye could say to you: this last clause is Rabbi Akiva’s, who says betrothal does not take effect with those liable for negative prohibitions. And it says that every prostitute with whom betrothal does not take effect, that is, forbidden relations and a gentile woman, like a widow to a High Priest, with whom betrothal does not take effect [according to him], her payment is forbidden; but a Jewish prostitute, with whom betrothal does take effect, her payment is permitted.

notes.he: ולרבא דאמר דאע"ג דתפסי קידושי [כמו] בזונה ישראלית אתננה אסור מאי שנא דקתני סיפא כגון אלמנה לכ"ג הא איהו סבר דכל זונה ישראלית אפי' פנויה דלא אסור לכהן אתננה אסור:
notes.en: And according to Rava, who says that even though betrothal takes effect, as with a Jewish prostitute, her payment is forbidden: why does the last clause teach specifically “for example, a widow to a High Priest”? He holds that the payment of every Jewish prostitute is forbidden, even an unmarried woman who is not forbidden to a priest.

notes.he: להכי קתני כגון אלמנה דסבר דומיא דאלמנה מה אלמנה אם בא עליה כהן בסתמא בלא התראה לא לקי אף זונה בסתמא אם בא עליה סתם ואח"כ נתן לה לא הוי אתנן [ולא הויא זונה] עד דאמר לה בפירוש הא ליך אתנן [וקבלתו לשם אתנן] ולאפוקי מדר' אלעזר דאמר עשאה זונה אפילו בסתם:
notes.en: Rava could say to you: it teaches “for example, a widow” because he holds [that a prostitute is] similar to a widow. Just as with a widow, if a priest had intercourse with her without specification, without warning, he is not flogged, so too a prostitute: if he had intercourse with her without specification and afterwards gave her [something], it is not payment [and she is not a prostitute] until he says to her explicitly, “Here is payment for you,” [and she accepted it as payment]. This excludes Rabbi Elazar, who says he has made her a prostitute even without specification.

notes.he: דזונה היא מעיקרא דכבר אמר לה אחר הא ליך אתנן וקיבלה אפילו בא עליה אחר בסתם ואח"כ נתן לה סתם אתננה אסור דהא הויא זונה מעיקרא:
notes.en: But where: she was a prostitute from the outset, because another man had already said to her, “Here is payment for you,” and she accepted it; then even if another man had intercourse with her without specification and afterwards gave her [something] without specification, her payment is forbidden, since she was a prostitute from the outset.

messages.text: With regard to one who says to another: Here is this lamb and in return your maidservant will lie with my slave and engage in intercourse with him, Rabbi Meir, or according to a different version of the text, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, says: The lamb’s halakhic status is not that of payment to a prostitute, and the Rabbis say: Its halakhic status is that of payment to a prostitute.
But a maidservant is permitted to a Canaanite slave. Since this is not an act of prostitution, why should the payment be prohibited?

notes.he: ואמאי קאמרי רבנן דהוי אתנן הא ליתא תנא דאסר אתנן המותרת אלא ר' אלעזר לחודיה:
notes.en: Is permitted: so why do the Rabbis say it is payment? There is no tanna who forbids the payment of a woman who is permitted [to the man] except Rabbi Elazar alone.

notes.he: ליה מאי איסור יש בזה אתנן או אמאי קרוי זה אתנן:
notes.en: But a maidservant is permitted to a slave: to him. What prohibition is there in this, that it should be payment? Why is this called payment?

messages.text: He means to say that the lamb is given for the maidservant to lie with him, the master, not the slave. And as for that which it teaches: Lie with my slave, he employs a euphemism.

notes.he: אצל הישראל עצמו ולדידיה אסורה שפחה:
notes.en: With him: with the Jew himself, and to him a maidservant is forbidden.

notes.he: ועבד היינו אבר המשמש כ"ש:
notes.en: A refined expression: and “slave” means the organ that serves [in intercourse]. [The note ends with an abbreviation, כ״ש, whose meaning here is unclear.]

notes.dh: אמר רב הונא (וסלין) [ותלין] אצל עצמו קאמר
notes.he: דהיינו איסורא ל"א מאן עבדי הוא עצמו כלומר (טלין) [ותלין] אצלי עמי קאמר והוא דקאמר עבדי לישנא מעליא קאמר כלומר דאינו רוצה לומר בפירוש ותלין עמי [א"כ דהוא עצמו קאמר אמאי קאמר ר' אינו אתנן הא יש בו איסור דישראל בעל שפחה אלא מאן עבדי דקאמר מתני' עבד עברי דמותר בשפחה כנענית אי הכי מאי טעמא דרבנן דאמרי דהוי אתנן]:
notes.en: Rav Huna said: he means “and let her lodge with him himself,” which is a prohibition. Another version: who is “my slave”? He himself; that is, he means “let her lodge with me,” and when he says “my slave” he uses a refined expression, that is, he does not want to say explicitly “let her lodge with me.” [If so, that he means himself, why does Rabbi say it is not payment? There is a prohibition here, of a Jew with a maidservant. Rather, the “my slave” of the mishna is a Hebrew slave, who is permitted to a Canaanite maidservant. If so, what is the reason of the Rabbis, who say it is payment?]

messages.text: If that is so, what is the reason for the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, who maintains that this payment is not prohibited?
messages.quote: with him, the master, not the slave

messages.text: Actually, the mishna is not employing a euphemism, and the master meant: My slave. And as for the difficulty that a maidservant is permitted to a slave, when the mishna teaches this case it is referring to a Hebrew slave, which is why Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi rules that the payment is permitted.
If so, what is the reason for the ruling of the Rabbis? After all, a maidservant is permitted to a Hebrew slave.

notes.he: דכתיב משנה שכר שכיר עבדך שעובד בין ביום ובין בלילה שהוליד לרבו בנים משפחתו:
notes.en: A maidservant is permitted to a Hebrew slave: as it is written: “For double the hire of a hired worker has he served you” (Deuteronomy 15:18): he works both by day and by night, for he fathered children for his master from his maidservant.

messages.text: Here we are dealing with a case where the Hebrew slave does not have a wife and children, and in that situation the Canaanite maidservant is not permitted to the Hebrew slave. As it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: לעבד עברי כדתניא יש לו לעבד עברי כשנכנס אשה ובנים רבו מוסר כו'. אין לו אשה ובנים אין רבו מוסר לו שפחה כנענית משום דכתב אם בגפו יבא בגפו יצא שלא היה לו אשה בגפו יצא שלא ימסור לו שפחה כנענית ואם מסר לו שאמר לחבירו הילך טלה ותלין שפחה אצל [עבדי] (עברי עברי) הוא זה אתנן דהוי איסור דהא לא הוה ליה אשה ובנים:
notes.en: For example, where he has no wife and children: the Hebrew slave. As it is taught: if the Hebrew slave had a wife and children when he entered [servitude], his master gives etc. If he has no wife and children, his master does not give him a Canaanite maidservant, because it is written: “If he came in by himself, he shall go out by himself” (Exodus 21:3): he had no wife; “he shall go out by himself”: that he should not give him a Canaanite maidservant. And if he gave her to him, and [a man] said to his fellow, “Here is a lamb, and let [your] maidservant lodge with my slave,” this is payment, for it is a prohibition, since he had no wife and children.

messages.text: If a Hebrew servant does not have a wife and children when he is enslaved, his master may not give him a Canaanite maidservant. If he has a wife and children, his master may give him a Canaanite maidservant.

notes.he: דכתיב אם בגפו יבא בגפו יצא ורבי דאמר לא הוי אתנן לית ליה האי סברא דודאי אפי' אין לו אשה ובנים מוסר לו רבו שפחה כנענית:
notes.en: His master does not give him etc.: as it is written: “If he came in by himself, he shall go out by himself” (Exodus 21:3). And Rabbi, who says it is not payment, does not hold this reasoning, for in his view, even if he has no wife and children, his master certainly may give him a Canaanite maidservant.

notes.dh: יש לו אשה ובנים רבו מוסר לו שפחה כנענית
notes.he: בעל כרחו של עבד דגזירת הכתוב היא דכתיב (שמות כ״א:ג׳) אם בעל אשה הוא וכתיב בתריה אם אדוניו יתן לו אשה וגו':
notes.en: If he has a wife and children, his master gives him a Canaanite maidservant: even against the slave’s will, for it is a decree of Scripture, as it is written: “If he is a married man” (Exodus 21:3), and after it is written: “If his master gives him a wife” (Exodus 21:4).

messages.text: By contrast, Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi maintains that the master may give a Canaanite maidservant to his Hebrew slave even if the slave does not have a wife and children, and therefore the relationship is not considered an act of prostitution.
Mishna

And which is the case where an animal has the halakhic status of the price of a dog, and it is therefore prohibited to sacrifice the animal on the altar? It is the case of one who says to another: Here is this lamb in place of a dog.

And likewise, this prohibition applies in the case of two partners who divided their common property, which included nineteen lambs and one dog, and one took ten lambs and the other one took nine lambs and a dog. Sacrifice of the ten lambs taken by the partner in exchange for the nine lambs and the dog is prohibited, and sacrifice of the nine lambs that were taken by the partner with the dog is permitted.

notes.he: להקרבה דמחיר כלב הן:
notes.en: Mishna. Those against the dog are forbidden: for sacrifice, since they are the price of a dog.

notes.he: אם שכנגד [הכלב] (כל) אסור כל העשרה דאמרינן כל חד וחד שייך כנגד הכלב כדמפרש בגמרא ואותן תשעה שעם הכלב מותרין:
notes.en: If those against the dog: all ten are forbidden, for we say that each and every one belongs against the dog, as is explained in the Gemara; and those nine that are with the dog are permitted.

messages.text: With regard to lambs given as payment to another for engaging in intercourse with his dog, or as the price of a prostitute to purchase her as his maidservant, their sacrifice is permitted, as it is stated: “As both of them are an abomination to the Lord your God” (Deuteronomy 23:19), from which it is inferred: Two are prohibited, payment to a prostitute and the price of a dog, and not four, i.e., the additional two cases of payment for intercourse with a dog and the price of a prostitute, which are permitted.

verse.he: לֹא־תָבִיא אֶתְנַן זוֹנָה וּמְחִיר כֶּלֶב בֵּית יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְכׇל־נֶדֶר כִּי תוֹעֲבַת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ גַּם־שְׁנֵיהֶם׃ {ס}
verse.en: You shall not bring the fee of a whore or the pay of a dog into the house of the ETERNAL your God in fulfillment of any vow, for both are abhorrent to the ETERNAL your God.

notes.he: הילך טלה זה ותלין כלבתך אצלי:
notes.en: Payment of a dog: [he says,] “Here is this lamb, and let your female dog spend the night with me.”

notes.he: שהחליף טלה בזונה וקנתה לשפחתו באותה טלה:
notes.en: The price of a prostitute: he exchanged a lamb for a prostitute, and acquired her as his maidservant with that lamb.

messages.text: Furthermore, with regard to the two prohibited cases of payment to a prostitute and the price of a dog, sacrifice of their offspring is permitted, as it is stated “them,” and not their offspring.

notes.he: דמחיר ואתנן:
notes.en: Their offspring: of the price and the payment.

notes.he: שנאמר שניהם ולא ולדותיהן:
notes.en: Are permitted: as it is said: “both of them,” and not their offspring.

messages.text: Gemara

“The price of a dog” (Deuteronomy 23:19), this is referring to an animal given in exchange for a dog. In this context the word “price” means an item given in exchange for another item, not money. And likewise the verse states: “You sell Your people without wealth, and have not set their prices high” (Psalms 44:13). The phrase “without wealth” indicates that the term “their prices” means an item given in exchange, rather than money.
messages.lead: With regard to the definition of the price of a dog, the Sages taught:

verse.en:
You sell Your people for no fortune,
You set no high price on them.

notes.he: אלמא מחיר היינו דמים:
notes.en: Gemara. “And have not set their prices high”: evidently meḥir, “price,” means damim, the value [given for something].

notes.he: בחלופיהם:
notes.en: “And have not set their prices high”: their exchanges.

messages.text: You can say instead that the verse: “Price of a dog,” is referring to payment to a prostitute, payment for intercourse with a dog, as well as the price of a dog.
messages.quote: this is referring to an animal given in exchange for a dog

notes.he: ממש דהא מחיר כלב היינו אתנן:
notes.en: Say instead payment: actual payment, so that “the price of a dog” is payment.

notes.he: אימא מאי מחיר כלב אתנן ממש דכלב כגון דאמר ליה הילך טלה זו ותלין שפחתך אצל כלבי:
notes.en: Say: what is “the price of a dog”? Actual payment for a dog, for example where he said to him: “Here is this lamb, and let your maidservant lodge with my dog.”

messages.text: One cannot explain the verse in this manner, as if so, there are three categories of items that may not be sacrificed to the altar, whereas the verse states: “Both of them,” indicating that there are two categories, and not three.

notes.he: [היינו אתנן זונה ואתנן ומחיר כלב]:
notes.en: And it answers: two and not three: [that is, payment of a prostitute, and payment and price of a dog].

notes.he: הוו להו תלתא אתנן זונה ואתנן כלב ומחיר כלב וגם שניהם כתב ולא שלשה:
notes.en: If so, there are three: payment of a prostitute, payment of a dog and price of a dog; yet it writes “both of them,” and not three.

messages.text: Did we say that payment to a prostitute, payment for intercourse with a dog, and the price of a dog should all be prohibited? We said that perhaps the phrase: The price of a dog, means the payment for intercourse with a dog, and not the price, i.e., the animal given in exchange for a dog. According to this suggestion, the verse indeed mentions only two categories: Payment given to a prostitute for services rendered, and payment for intercourse with a dog.

notes.he: ומאן דאמר אימא [כו'] אמר לך ליכא למיפרך שנים ולא שלשה דמי קא אמרינן (אמאי) [אנן] אתנן ומחיר כלומר דאתנן נמי (דהא) משמע אכלב (כלב) דהיינו שלשה אתנן ולא מחיר קאמרינן כלומר דמאי מחיר אתנן כלב והיינו שנים:
notes.en: And the one who said “say [etc.]” would answer you: there is no refutation from “two and not three.” Do we say payment and price, that is, that “payment” also applies to the dog, which would make three? We are saying payment and not price, that is: what is “price”? Payment of a dog. That makes two.

messages.text: If that is so, let the verse state: You shall not bring the payment to a prostitute or a dog, as in this formulation the word “payment” refers both to the prostitute and the dog.

notes.he: כדאמרת מאי מחיר כלב נימא קרא אתנן זונה וכלב דהוה משמע נמי אתנן אכלב אלא מדכתב רחמנא אתנן זונה ומחיר כלב ש"מ מחיר הוא דקאמר רחמנא אכלב דהיינו חילוף ולא אתנן:
notes.en: If so: as you said, what is “the price of a dog”? [Payment.] Then let the verse say “the payment of a prostitute or a dog,” which would also imply payment for the dog. Rather, since the Merciful One wrote “the payment of a prostitute and the price of a dog,” learn from it that “price” is what the Merciful One says about the dog, which means an exchange, and not payment.

messages.text: From the fact that it is written: “The payment of a harlot or the price of a dog,” one can learn from here that the verse is referring to two different matters: Payment to a prostitute, and an animal exchanged for a dog.

notes.he: כלומר מדכתיב וי"ו גבי ומחיר מוסיף על ענין ראשון ובין חליפיו ובין אתננו אסור:
notes.en: “And the price of a dog” is written: that is, since the vav is written with “and the price,” it adds to the first matter, and both its exchange and its payment are forbidden.

notes.he: ל"א מחיר כלב היינו אתננה דכלב ולא חילוף:
notes.en: Another version: “the price of a dog” is the payment of a dog, and not an exchange.

notes.he: א"כ נכתב קרא אתנן זונה וכלב ולא בעי מחיר ואימא אתנן זונה ומחיר כלב דוי"ו דומחיר נוסף על ענין ראשון וקרי ביה הכי אתנן ומחיר כלב כלומר דשם דאתנן ומחיר תרוייהו חלין על כלב:
notes.en: If so, let the verse write “the payment of a prostitute or a dog,” with no need for “price.” [Answer:] say [that it reads] “the payment of a prostitute and the price of a dog,” for the vav of “and the price” adds to the first matter, and read it thus: “the payment and the price of a dog”; that is, that the name of both payment and price apply to a dog.

notes.he: תועבת ה' גם שניהם כתב שנים ולא שלשה ואי כדאמרת הוו שלשה אתנן זונה ואתנן ומחיר דכלב:
notes.en: That cannot enter your mind: “an abomination to the Lord… both of them” it writes, two and not three. And if it were as you said, there would be three: payment of a prostitute, and payment and price of a dog.

messages.text: With regard to two partners who divided their common property, and one took ten lambs and the other one took nine lambs and a dog, sacrifice of the ten lambs taken by the partner in exchange for nine lambs and a dog is prohibited.
messages.quote: two partners who divided their common property, and one took ten lambs

messages.text: Why should all ten lambs be prohibited? Let us remove one of the lambs corresponding to the dog, and all the rest of these lambs will be permitted.

notes.he: פירוש מטעם ברירה והשתא ניחא לפר"י דפסק הילכתא בכולי הש"ס דיש ברירה אבל לר"ת דפסק הילכתא דאין ברירה היכי פריך כ"כ בפשיטות ואידך לישתרו וי"ל משום דאיכא תנאי דאית להו ברירה פריך ליה ממתני' דלא כוותיה מיתוקמא יש לתמוה דהכא משמע שאם איסור מעורב בהיתר נוטל האיסור וסומכין על ברירה לומר שזהו האיסור שנסתלק לכן בההיא דהלוקח יין מבין הכותים (דמאי פ"ז מ"ד) שני לוגין שאני עתיד להפריש הרי הן מעשר וסומך על ברירה ולומר שזהו החולין שהוא שותה וכן ההיא דג' שלקחו קיניהן בשותפות ומתה אחת מהן דפריך הש"ס בפשיטות במס' יומא (דף נה:) ונשקול ד' זוזי ונישדינהו ואידך לישתרו משום ברירה וא"כ בכל איסור המעורב בהיתר נסמוך אברירה ונשקול כשיעור האיסור ואידך לישתרו וכן זבחים שנתערבו בשור הנסקל דאמרינן (זבחים דף ע:) ימותו ואמאי נהי דבעלי חיים חשיבי ולא בטלי מ"מ נשקול חד מינייהו ואידך לישתרו ואומר מורי הרמ"ר כלל גדול בדין זה דודאי כל דבר שהוברר האיסור מתחלה ואח"כ נתערב בהיתר לא סמכינן אברירה כיון שתערובתו היה באיסור אבל הני תערובתן בהיתר כי האיסור לא היה מבורר קודם תערובתו ולאחר התערובת נולד האיסור אז סמכינן אברירה: [ועי' היטב תוספות בכורות נו: ושייך לדף נז. ד"ה לברור וע"ע תוספות סוטה יח. ד"ה חזר]
notes.en:
In brief: “And let the rest be permitted”: that is, by the principle of bererah, retroactive clarification. This fits the Ri, who rules throughout the Talmud that bererah applies; but according to Rabbeinu Tam, who rules that it does not, how can the Gemara ask so simply? Answer: since there are tanna’im who hold bererah, it asks why the mishna should be established against them.
A further difficulty: here it implies that when a forbidden item is mixed with permitted ones, one takes out the forbidden amount and relies on bererah to say that this is the forbidden one that was removed, as in one who buys wine from the Samaritans and says “two log that I will separate are tithe” (Demai 7:4), relying on bererah that what he drinks is non-sacred; and as with the three women who bought their pairs of birds in partnership, one of which died, where the Gemara asks simply in Yoma (55b), “Let us take four zuz and throw them away, and let the rest be permitted.” If so, for every forbidden item mixed with permitted ones we should rely on bererah, take out the forbidden amount and let the rest be permitted. And with offerings mixed with an ox that is to be stoned, where we say they must all die (Zevaḥim 70b): granted that living creatures are significant and are not nullified, still let us take one of them and let the rest be permitted!
My teacher HaRaMaR says a great rule in this: wherever the forbidden item was identified first and afterwards mixed with permitted ones, we do not rely on bererah, since it was mixed as a forbidden item. But in these cases the mixture was of permitted things, for the forbidden item was not identified before it was mixed, and the prohibition came into being after the mixture; then we rely on bererah. [See Tosafot Bekhorot 56b, and Tosafot Sota 18a.] Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: ל"א אמאי אסורי' כולן שכנגד הכלב לישקול חד מהנהו דבהדי כלבא דתיתסר ואינך לישתרו:
notes.en: Another version: why are all those against the dog forbidden? Let one take one of those that are with the dog to be forbidden, and let the rest be permitted.

messages.text: Here we are dealing with a case where the value of the dog is worth more than each one of the ten lambs seperately. Therefore, one cannot set aside one of the lambs in exchange for the dog. And consequently, one casts this addition of the value of the dog between all of the lambs. As a result, all ten lambs are prohibited, since the price of the dog is included in each of them.

notes.he: שאין באותן שכנגדו שום טלה ששוה דמי הכלב דהשתא דמי הכלב מעורבין בכולהו. כגון שאותן שכנגדו שוה כל חד וחד דינר דהוו עשרה דינרין ואותן תשעה שעמו שוין כל חד דינר חסר מעה דהיינו תשעה דינרין פחות תשעה מעות והכלב שוה דינר ותשעה מעות הרי י' דינרים נמצא בתשעה מאותן שכנגדו מגיע מדמי הכלב והעשירי כולו כנגדו. לשון ירושלמי כגון דשוי לכל חד וחד מאותן שכנגדו ארבע זוזי ופלגי חומשא דזוזא דהוו להו בין כולהו מ"א זוזא ואותן שעמו לא שוו כל חד אלא ד' זוזי דהוו שלשים ושש זוזי וכלבא שוי חמשא והוו מ"א נמצא בתשעה מעשרה שכנגדו בכל אחד חצי חומש מדמי הכלב והעשירי כולו כנגדו:
notes.en:
Than one of them: that among those set against it there is no lamb worth the dog’s value, so that now the dog’s value is mixed into all of them. For example, those set against it are each worth a dinar, making ten dinars, and the nine with it are each worth a dinar less a ma’ah, that is, nine dinars less nine ma’ot, and the dog is worth a dinar and nine ma’ot: that makes ten dinars. It follows that in nine of those set against it [part] of the dog’s value is found, and the tenth is wholly against it.
In the language of the Jerusalem Talmud: for example, each of those set against it is worth four zuz and half a fifth of a zuz, making forty-one zuz among them all, and those with it are worth only four zuz each, making thirty-six zuz, and the dog is worth five, making forty-one. It follows that in each of nine of the ten set against it there is half a fifth of the dog’s value, and the tenth is wholly against it.

notes.dh: הכא במאי עסקינן כגון דאיטפי דמי כלבא מכל חד מנייהו
notes.he: דשכנגדו דההוא טופיינא דכלב שייך בכולהו לאשלומי הילכך שכנגד הכלב כולן אסורין:
notes.en: Here we are dealing with: for example, where the dog’s value exceeds each one of them that are set against it, so that the dog’s excess belongs to all of them, to make up its value. Therefore all those set against the dog are forbidden.

notes.dh: אמר רב אשי הכא במאי עסקינן
notes.he: כגון דשוויין כולהו עשרה אימראין כל חד וחד ד' זוזי ופלגי דחומשא וכלבא שוי ה' זוזי דזוזא יתירא דכלבא אותו חמישי משיך בכולהון דפלגו חומשא דכולהו סליק לחד (חומש) [זוז] היינו אותו זוז חמישי שהכלב שוי יותר. והאי לישנא בתרא מפרש טופיינא דלישנא קמא:
notes.en: Rav Ashi said: here we are dealing with [a case] where each of all ten lambs is worth four zuz and half a fifth, and the dog is worth five zuz, so that the dog’s extra zuz, that fifth one, extends into all of them; for the half-fifths of all of them come to one zuz, which is that fifth zuz by which the dog is worth more. And this last version explains the “excess” of the first version. [Rabbeinu Gershom’s text gives this answer in the name of Rav Ashi; on the daf it is unattributed.]

messages.caption: Rashi’s two examples of a dog worth more than any one lamb, so that its value is spread among the ten lambs.

messages.text: With regard to animals given as payment to another for engaging in intercourse with a dog, or as the price of a prostitute to purchase her as his maidservant, their sacrifice is permitted. Rava from Parzakya said to Rav Ashi:
messages.quote: payment to another for engaging in intercourse with his dog, or as the price of a prostitute

notes.he: כגון שהחליף טלה בזונה הרי אלו מותרין שנים שנים ולא ארבעה והיינו ארבעה אתנן זונה ואתנן כלב מחיר זונה ומחיר כלב:
notes.en: Payment of a dog, as we said, and the price of a prostitute, for example where he exchanged a lamb for a prostitute: these are permitted. “Two”: two and not four. The four are payment of a prostitute, payment of a dog, price of a prostitute and price of a dog.

messages.text: @Rav Ashi From where is this matter that the Sages stated, that there is no prostitution with regard to an animal derived? I.e., from where is it derived that a woman who copulates with an animal is not considered a prostitute, in accordance with the ruling of the mishna that payment for intercourse with an animal is permitted?

notes.he: דקתני מתני' אתנן כלב מותר:
notes.en: There is no prostitution with an animal: as the mishna teaches, payment of a dog is permitted.

notes.dh: מנא הא מילתא דאמרי רבנן אין זנות לבהמה
notes.he: דקתני במתני' אתנן כלב מותר לשון רש"י וקשיא וכי לא היה יודע דמתני' קרא דריש דב' ולא ד' ועוד מאי קמהדר לא לישתמיט כו' וכי (לא) היה ר"ל סברא חדשה שאינה במשנה ועוד כי מייתי ברייתא דב' ולא ד' אמאי לא מייתי מתני' דקתני נמי הכי ונראה למורי דודאי רב אחא מפרזיקא היה יודע המשנה והפסוק דב' ולא ד' והיה פשיטא ליה דאם היה נותן האתנן לכלבתא דאינו אתנן משום קרא דשנים ולא ארבעה אבל היה בעי להפך אם אדם נותן אתנן לזונה על מנת שילין כלבו אצלה אם ביאת כלב מיקריא ביאת זנות או לא ואע"ג דאין אתנן שאדם נותן לכלבתא אסור מ"מ אתנן שנותן כלב לאשה אסור ומשני לא לשתמיט תנא דליתני אתנן שנותן אדם לה ואתנן שהכלב נותן לה והלשון דחוק קצת ובתר הכי מייתי מן הברייתא דכי היכי דאמר דאין ביאת אדם בבהמה ביאת זנות כך אין ביאת בהמה באשה קרויה זנות וממתני' לא רצה להביא משום דמשנה אין דרכה לפרש אבל ברייתא אם היה אתנן אשה הנבעלת לכלב אסור היה לה לפרש וביבמות (דף נט:) מוכיח דמילתא דרב אחא נאמר על אשה שנבעלה לכלב דאיכא התם מעשה בריבה אחת בהיתלו שהיתה מכבדת ורבעה כלב כופרי מאחוריה בא מעשה לפני חכמי' והכשירוה ועל המעשה בעא רב אחא מפרזיקיא מנא הא מילתא:
notes.en:
In brief: Rashi explains that the question concerns the mishna’s ruling that payment of a dog is permitted. This is difficult: did he not know that the mishna expounds the verse, “two and not four”? And what is the answer “the verse would not have omitted…”: was Rav Ashi giving a new reasoning not found in the mishna? And when the Gemara cites the baraita of “two and not four,” why not cite the mishna, which teaches the same?
My teacher’s view: Rav Aḥa from Parzakya [so Tosafot read the name] certainly knew the mishna and the verse, and it was obvious to him that payment given for a female dog is not payment, because of “two and not four.” But he was asking the reverse: if a man gives a woman payment so that his dog may lie with her, is intercourse with a dog called intercourse of prostitution or not? Even though payment that a man gives for a female dog is not forbidden, perhaps payment for a dog’s intercourse with a woman is forbidden. And it answers: the verse would not have failed to write “the payment of a prostitute or a dog,” [covering] both the payment a man gives her and the payment for a dog with her. The wording is somewhat forced.
Then it cites the baraita: just as a man’s intercourse with an animal is not intercourse of prostitution, so an animal’s with a woman is not called prostitution. It did not cite the mishna, because a mishna does not usually explain; but a baraita would have said so explicitly had the payment of a woman who was with a dog been forbidden. And in Yevamot (59b) it is evident that Rav Aḥa’s statement was said about a woman with a dog: there is an incident there of a young woman in Hitlu who was sweeping the house, and a dog copulated with her from behind; the case came before the Sages and they ruled her fit [to marry a priest], and about that incident Rav Aḥa from Parzakya asked, “From where is this matter…?” Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: לאסור אתננה:
notes.en: There is no prostitution with an animal: to forbid its payment.

messages.text: There was nothing preventing the verse from writing: You shall not bring the payment of a prostitute or a dog into the House of the Lord your God. Since the verse states: “You shall not bring the payment of a prostitute or the price of a dog,” this indicates that these are two different cases, and there is no prostitution with regard to an animal.
messages.lead: Rav Ashi said to Rava from Parzakya:
messages.quote: there is no prostitution with regard to an animal

notes.he: לא לישתמיט קרא ולכתב אתנן זונה וכלב דאתנן נמי משוי אכלב. ל"א מדלא כתב אתנן ומחיר כלב וזונה דלא משוי אתנן ומחיר אכלב ואזונה:
notes.en: For if it were so, the verse would not have omitted to write “the payment of a prostitute or a dog,” so that “payment” would apply to the dog too. Another version: since it did not write “the payment and the price of a dog and of a prostitute,” it does not apply payment and price both to the dog and to the prostitute.

messages.text: This is also taught in a baraita:

notes.he: גרסי' לה. [מתניתין היא אלא משום דתני בברייתא מנין לאתנן כו' ומפרשה בהדיא להכי מייתי לה וגמגום ונ"ל דלא גרסינן לה]:
notes.en: It is also taught so: “From where” etc.: we read this. [It is the mishna; but because the baraita teaches “From where is it for payment…” and explains it explicitly, he cites it for that reason. This is uncertain, and it seems to me that we do not read it.]

notes.he: דאין זנות בבהמה:
notes.en: It is also taught so: that there is no prostitution with an animal.

messages.text: From where is it derived with regard to the payment of a lamb to another for engaging in intercourse with a dog, or as the price of a prostitute to purchase her as his maidservant, that their sacrifice is permitted? As it is stated: “For even both of them are an abomination to the Lord your God” (Deuteronomy 23:19), from which it is inferred: Two are prohibited, payment to a prostitute and the price of a dog, and not four, i.e., payment for intercourse with a dog and the price of a prostitute, which are permitted.

verse.he: לֹא־תָבִיא אֶתְנַן זוֹנָה וּמְחִיר כֶּלֶב בֵּית יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְכׇל־נֶדֶר כִּי תוֹעֲבַת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ גַּם־שְׁנֵיהֶם׃ {ס}
verse.en: You shall not bring the fee of a whore or the pay of a dog into the house of the ETERNAL your God in fulfillment of any vow, for both are abhorrent to the ETERNAL your God.

notes.he: דאם תאמר כן ליתן את האמור של זה בזה אתנן כלב ומחיר זונה דאסורין א"כ הוו להו ארבעה:
notes.en: For if you say so, to apply what is said of this one to that one, so that payment of a dog and price of a prostitute are forbidden, there would be four.

messages.text: Furthermore, sacrifice of their offspring is permitted, as it is stated: “Even both of them,” which indicates that it is “them” that are forbidden, and not their offspring.

notes.he: של אתנן ומחיר מותרין:
notes.en: And their offspring: of the payment and the price, are permitted.

notes.he: הם ולא וולדותיהן:
notes.en: As it is said, “even both of them”: them, and not their offspring.

messages.text: The offspring of a female animal that was the object of bestiality when it was pregnant is prohibited to be sacrificed on the altar, like its mother. The reason is that it is considered as though it, the mother, and its offspring both were the object of bestiality. Likewise, if a pregnant cow gores and kills a Jew, its offspring is prohibited to be sacrificed, like its mother, as it is as though it, the mother, and its offspring both gored.
messages.lead: The Gemara discusses other cases of offspring of animals with regard to sacrifice on the altar.

messages.text: But the offspring of a set-aside animal and an animal worshipped as an idol are permitted to be sacrificed on the altar. What is the reason? It is that only the mother was set aside, and not the offspring. Likewise, they worshipped only its mother, not the offspring.

notes.he: דלא אקצייה אלא לדידה ולא פלחא אלא לדידה:
notes.en: The offspring of a set-aside and a worshipped animal is permitted: for he set aside only the mother, and they worshipped only the mother.

notes.he: כלומר לא נתכוון להקצות אלא לאמו ולא לעובר:
notes.en: What is the reason? He set aside its mother: that is, he intended to set aside only its mother and not the fetus.

messages.text: The offspring of a set-aside animal and the offspring of an animal worshipped as an idol are prohibited. What is the reason? It is that it is beneficial to the owner if its girth is large, as a pregnant animal is more impressive than an ordinary one. Consequently, its offspring is also considered set-aside and worshipped, and it is therefore prohibited.
messages.lead: There are those who say a different version of Rava’s statement:

notes.he: תימה דהכא גבי נעבד אסרינן ולד נעבד ובמס' ע"ז (דף מו:) בעי המשתחוה לקמה סולת מהו למנחות יש שינוי בנעבד או אין שינוי בנעבד ומייתי הך מילתא דרבא דולד נעבד אסור ומשני התם מעיקרא בהמה והשתא בהמה ובבא הוא דאחידא באפיה אבל סולת מעיקרא חיטין והשתא סולת אלמא שרינן טפי בשינוי מבנולד וגבי אתנן הוי סברא דב"ש להפך דאמרו שינוי במקומו הוא עומד וחיטין ועשאן סולת אסורין ובולד מודו דשרי מדרשא דהם ולא ולדותיהם ויש טעם לחלק דודאי גבי עבודת כוכבים ולד אסור כדמפרש הכא דניחא ליה בנפחיה ודעתו להשתחוות לכל הנפח אבל משתחוה לקמה אין דעתו להשתחוות אלא למה שהוא רואה דהיינו את החיטין ולא את הסולת אבל גבי אתנן דעתה אעיקר והעילוי לפיכך גבי בהמה דדעת הזונה לבהמה ולא לולד וגבי קמה דעתה לסולת שהיא עיקר:
notes.en:
That he is pleased with its girth: this is puzzling. Here, with a worshipped animal, we forbid the offspring of a worshipped animal; and in Avoda Zara (46b) it asks: one who bows down to standing grain, what is [its] fine flour for meal offerings? Does a change [of form] apply to a worshipped item or not? And it cites this statement of Rava, that the offspring of a worshipped animal is forbidden, and answers there: at first it was an animal and now it is an animal, it was merely that a door was closed before it; but fine flour was at first wheat and is now fine flour. Evidently we are more lenient with a change than with an offspring. Yet with a prostitute’s payment, the reasoning of Beit Shammai is the reverse: they said that a change stays as it was, and wheat that was made into fine flour is forbidden, while for offspring they agree it is permitted, from the exposition “them, and not their offspring.”
There is a reason to distinguish. Certainly with idolatry the offspring is forbidden, as explained here, that he is pleased with its girth and intends to bow down to the whole girth; but one who bows down to standing grain intends to bow down only to what he sees, the wheat, and not the fine flour. With a payment, however, her intent is for the principal and its increase in value; therefore with an animal, the prostitute’s intent is for the animal and not the offspring, and with grain, her intent is for the fine flour, which is the main thing.

notes.he: [מוקצה [ונעבד] אסור] (וולד כדבעי אסור) שהעובר נהנה ממה שהאם נהנית:
notes.en: [The offspring of a] set-aside [and worshipped animal] is forbidden: for the fetus benefits from what its mother benefits.

notes.he: כלומר דניחא ליה כשהבהמה מעוברת נראית שמינה ונפוחה ונראית חשובה יותר לעבודת כוכבים הילכך ניחא ליה בעובר (כעובר) ואסור:
notes.en: What is the reason? He is pleased with its swelling and fattening: that is, he is pleased that when the animal is pregnant it looks fat and swollen and appears more important for idol worship. Therefore he is pleased with the fetus, and it is forbidden.

messages.text: With regard to one who betroths a woman with the excrement of an ox that is sentenced to be stoned, if the excrement is worth at least one peruta, the woman is betrothed. Although it is not permitted to derive benefit from the ox itself, one may derive benefit from its excrement. But if one betroths her with the excrement of calves that were used for idol worship, she is not betrothed, as even their excrement is prohibited.
messages.lead: Rav Aḥadevoi bar Ami says that Rav says:

messages.text: What is the reason for the difference between the excrement of an ox that is stoned and the excrement of calves used for idolatry? If you wish, say that this is learned from a verse; if you wish, say instead that it is derived by means of a logical argument.

If you wish, say it is derived by means of a logical argument: With regard to calves used for idol worship, a calf’s additional girth due to the excrement stored in its body is beneficial to the owner, as fatter animals are more impressive. Therefore, the excrement is considered part of the offering and is prohibited. By contrast, with regard to an ox that is stoned, its additional girth is not beneficial to him, as he gains nothing from it, and consequently it is not considered part of the animal.

notes.he: איב"א סברא גבי ע"ז ניחא ליה בנפחיה בפרש שיש בו שנראית שמינה הילכך אסור בהנאה:
notes.en: If you wish, say it is reasoning: with idol worship he is pleased with its girth, from the excrement inside it, which makes it look fat; therefore [the excrement] is forbidden for benefit.

notes.dh: בשור הנסקל לא ניחא ליה בניפחיה
notes.he: בפרשו שהרי עומד למות הילכך מקודשת:
notes.en: With an ox that is to be stoned, he is not pleased with its girth from its excrement, for it is about to die; therefore she is betrothed.

messages.text: If you wish, say that this is learned from a verse: It is written with regard to an animal used for idol worship: “And you shall not bring an abomination into your house, and be [vehayita] accursed like it” (Deuteronomy 7:26). This teaches that anything that you create [mehayye] from the idol is prohibited like the idol itself.

verse.he: וְלֹא־תָבִיא תוֹעֵבָה אֶל־בֵּיתֶךָ וְהָיִיתָ חֵרֶם כָּמֹהוּ שַׁקֵּץ ׀ תְּשַׁקְּצֶנּוּ וְתַעֵב ׀ תְּתַעֲבֶנּוּ כִּי־חֵרֶם הוּא׃ {פ}
verse.en: You must not bring an abhorrent thing into your house, or you will be proscribed like it; you must reject it as abominable and abhorrent, for it is proscribed.

notes.dh: כל שאתה מהיה ממנו הרי הוא (אסור) כמוהו
notes.he: כל הבא ממנו אסור ואינה מקודשת:
notes.en: Anything that you create from it is like it: anything that comes from it is forbidden, and she is not betrothed.

messages.text: But with regard to an ox that is stoned, it is written: “The ox shall surely be stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten” (Exodus 21:28). This teaches that only its flesh is forbidden, but its excrement is permitted.

verse.he: וְכִי־יִגַּח שׁוֹר אֶת־אִישׁ אוֹ אֶת־אִשָּׁה וָמֵת סָקוֹל יִסָּקֵל הַשּׁוֹר וְלֹא יֵאָכֵל אֶת־בְּשָׂרוֹ וּבַעַל הַשּׁוֹר נָקִי׃
verse.en: When an ox gores a man or a woman to death, the ox shall be stoned and its flesh shall not be eaten, but the owner of the ox is not to be punished.

messages.text: Mishna

If one gave money to a prostitute as her payment, it is permitted to purchase an offering with that money, as the money itself is not sacrificed. If he paid her with wine, or oil, or flour, or any other item the like of which is sacrificed on the altar, sacrifice of those items is prohibited.
If he gave her consecrated items for her services, their sacrifice is permitted. Since they were already consecrated, they do not belong to him, and one cannot prohibit an item that is not his.

notes.he: לא חייל עלייהו אתנן כדמפרש בגמ':
notes.en: Mishna. He gave her consecrated items: payment does not take effect on them, as is explained in the Gemara.

messages.text: If he paid her with non-sacred birds, their sacrifice is prohibited.

notes.he: חולין הרי אלו אסורין שוב להקרבה:
notes.en: He gave her birds: non-sacred ones; these are thereafter forbidden for sacrifice.

messages.text: As, by right, it should be inferred a fortiori: If in the case of consecrated items, which a blemish disqualifies, the prohibition of payment to a prostitute and the price of a dog do not take effect with regard to them; with regard to a bird, which a blemish does not disqualify, is it not right that the prohibition of payment to a prostitute and the price of a dog should not take effect with regard to them? Therefore, the verse states: “You shall not bring the payment of a prostitute, or the price of a dog, into the House of the Lord your God for any vow” (Deuteronomy 23:19). This serves to include the bird in the prohibition.

verse.he: לֹא־תָבִיא אֶתְנַן זוֹנָה וּמְחִיר כֶּלֶב בֵּית יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְכׇל־נֶדֶר כִּי תוֹעֲבַת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ גַּם־שְׁנֵיהֶם׃ {ס}
verse.en: You shall not bring the fee of a whore or the pay of a dog into the house of the ETERNAL your God in fulfillment of any vow, for both are abhorrent to the ETERNAL your God.

messages.text: With regard to all animals whose sacrifice on the altar is prohibited, sacrifice of their offspring is permitted.
The offspring of an animal with a wound that will cause it to die within twelve months [tereifa] shall not be sacrificed on the altar.

notes.he: אבל להדיוט ד"ה מותר דלאו מגופה קא רבי:
notes.en: The offspring of a tereifa shall not be sacrificed: but for an ordinary person all agree it is permitted, since it did not grow from its body.

notes.dh: רבי אליעזר אומר ולד טרפה לא יקרב
notes.he: פרש"י אבל להדיוט ד"ה שרי דלא מגופה קא רבו ולא נהירא דבפ' אלו טרפות (חולין נח.) מפרש בהדיא דאפי' להדיוט נמי אסור והא דפליגי לגבוה (נמי שרי) להודיעך (כחן דרבנן) דאפי' לגבוה נמי שרו לכך נראה דאף להדיוט אסור והא דנקט לא יקרב משום רבנן דאמרי יקרב נקטיה:
notes.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: the offspring of a tereifa shall not be sacrificed: Rashi explains that for an ordinary person all agree it is permitted, since it did not grow from its body. This is not correct, for in chapter Elu Tereifot (Ḥullin 58a) it is explained explicitly that it is forbidden even to an ordinary person, and that they disagree about the altar is to tell you the strength of the Rabbis’ view, that they permit it even for the altar. Therefore it seems that [according to Rabbi Eliezer] it is forbidden even to an ordinary person, and he says “shall not be sacrificed” because of the Rabbis, who say “it may be sacrificed.”

messages.text: A kosher animal that suckled from a tereifa is disqualified from sacrifice on the altar.

With regard to all sacrificial animals that became tereifot, one may not redeem them and render them non-sacred, as their consumption is forbidden and one does not redeem sacrificial animals to feed them to dogs, as this is considered a degradation of sacrificial animals.
Gemara
If one gave wheat to a prostitute and she made the wheat into flour, or if he gave her olives and she made them into oil, or if he gave her grapes and she made them into wine,

it is taught in one baraita that these products are prohibited to be used as an offering in the Temple, and it is taught in another baraita that they are permitted, as the physical change transforms them into new objects.
Beit Shammai prohibit these products and Beit Hillel permit them.

notes.he: שם מקום:
notes.en: Aspork: the name of a place.

messages.text: If so, the two baraitot cited above reflect a dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel.

Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel both derive their ruling from the verse: “You shall not bring the hire of a harlot, or the price of a dog, into the House of the Lord your God for any vow; for even both of them are an abomination to the Lord your God” (Deuteronomy 23:19). Beit Hillel, who permit these items after they have undergone a physical change, maintain that the word “them” teaches that this prohibition applies only to the original items, but not to their offspring. Likewise, it applies only to them, i.e., the items in their original form, but not to their changed status.

verse.he: לֹא־תָבִיא אֶתְנַן זוֹנָה וּמְחִיר כֶּלֶב בֵּית יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְכׇל־נֶדֶר כִּי תוֹעֲבַת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ גַּם־שְׁנֵיהֶם׃ {ס}
verse.en: You shall not bring the fee of a whore or the pay of a dog into the house of the ETERNAL your God in fulfillment of any vow, for both are abhorrent to the ETERNAL your God.

messages.text: Beit Shammai maintain that one indeed derives: “Them,” but not their offspring. But they maintain that the word “even” serves to include in the prohibition items in their changed status.

notes.he: כלומר כל מה שלקוח מאתנן ועוד דאי אמרת מה שלקחה בהמה מאתננה אסור א"כ היינו ולדותיהן שבא מן האתנן ומתניתין קתני ולדותיהן מותרי'. אמר קרא גם שניהם הם ולא ולדותיהן. גם היינו רבויא לרבות שינוייהם כגון חיטין ועשאתן סולת אע"ג דנשתנו אסורין:
notes.en: [It seems that Rabbeinu Gershom read here in the Gemara: “What is the reason that if he gave her money they are permitted?”] For it is written “payment of a prostitute,” and not “the payment”; and it is not written “with payment,” that is, anything bought with the payment. Moreover, if you said that an animal she bought with her payment is forbidden, that would be like their offspring, which come from the payment, and the mishna teaches that their offspring are permitted: the verse says “even both of them,” them and not their offspring. “Even” is an inclusion, to include their changed forms, such as wheat that she made into fine flour: even though they changed, they are forbidden.

messages.text: And according to the opinion of Beit Hillel, isn’t it written “even”? How do they interpret that word?
The word “even” is in fact difficult according to Beit Hillel.

notes.he: שניהם הם ולא שינויהם ושינוייהם ולדותיהם מותרים וגם דאמרינן דאתי לרבות קשיא לב"ה דהא לא קא מרבי מידי מיניה:
notes.en: And Beit Hillel expound thus: “both of them”: them, and not their changed forms; their changed forms and their offspring are permitted. And “even,” which we said comes to include, is difficult for Beit Hillel, since for them it includes nothing.

messages.text: With regard to the verse: “You shall not bring the hire of a harlot, or the price of a dog, into the House of the Lord your God,” this excludes a red heifer, which is not brought to the House of the Lord, i.e., the Temple, but is slaughtered outside Jerusalem on the Mount of Olives. This is the statement of Rabbi Elazar.

verse.he: לֹא־תָבִיא אֶתְנַן זוֹנָה וּמְחִיר כֶּלֶב בֵּית יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְכׇל־נֶדֶר כִּי תוֹעֲבַת יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ גַּם־שְׁנֵיהֶם׃ {ס}
verse.en: You shall not bring the fee of a whore or the pay of a dog into the house of the ETERNAL your God in fulfillment of any vow, for both are abhorrent to the ETERNAL your God.

notes.he: אדומה:
notes.en: A heifer: the red one.

notes.he: דכל מעשיה עושין בהר המשחה דמותרת להביא מאתנן:
notes.en: Excluding a heifer, which does not come into the House: for all its rites are done on the Mount of Anointing, so one may bring it from a payment.

messages.text: This verse serves to include in the prohibition beaten plates of gold in the Temple, if the gold was used as payment to a prostitute or as the price of a dog.

notes.he: ציפוי למזבח אם נתן לה זהב:
notes.en: And plates: overlay for the altar, if he gave her gold.

notes.he: שאין מביאין מאתנן אפי' אחרי בית הכפרת מבחוץ לטוח הקיר דהתם נמי קרינן ביה בית ה':
notes.en: And the Rabbis say: “House” includes the plates: that one does not bring [them] from a payment, even behind the Hall of the Ark Cover, outside, to plaster the wall, for there too we call it “the House of the Lord.”

messages.text: Who are the Rabbis cited here?
messages.quote: to include in the prohibition beaten plates of gold

messages.text: It is the opinion of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, as it is taught in a baraita:

One may not fashion hanging beaten plates of gold for the Temple from it, even for the area behind the Hall of the Ark Cover, i.e., the eleven cubits of space behind the Holy of Holies up to the wall of the Temple courtyard, which was at the western end of the Sanctuary. Athough this area is of lesser sanctity than the rest of the Temple, one may not place there any gold given as payment to a prostitute.
messages.lead: If one gave a prostitute gold as her payment, Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:

notes.he: דאמרינן בפ"ק דיומא (דף כא.) י"א אמה היו נותרים בעזרה אחורי חומת בית הכפורת דאפילו התם דקילא קדושתה אסור האתנן אם יש בנין לעשות והוא נתן לה אבנים באתננה:
notes.en: Behind the Hall of the Ark Cover: as we say in the first chapter of Yoma (21a), eleven cubits were left in the courtyard behind the wall of the Hall of the Ark Cover. Even there, where the sanctity is lighter, payment is forbidden, if there is building to be done and he gave her stones as her payment.

messages.text: If he gave her consecrated items for her services, their sacrifice is permitted, whereas if he paid her with non-sacred birds, their sacrifice is prohibited. The prohibited status of birds is derived from the verse: “You shall not bring the hire of a harlot, or the price of a dog, into the House of the Lord your God for any vow,” despite an a fortiori inference from consecrated animals that indicates they should be permitted.
messages.quote: If he gave her consecrated items for her services, their sacrifice is permitted

notes.dh: נתן לה מוקדש' באתננה הרי אלו מותרין
notes.he: ועופות הרי אלו אסור' שהיה בדין שהעופות יהו מותרין:
notes.en: He gave her consecrated items as her payment, they are permitted; and birds are forbidden, though by right the birds should have been permitted.

notes.he: להביא את העוף שבא בנדר ונדבה שאתנן חל עליהן:
notes.en: The verse states “for any vow”: to include the bird, which comes as a vow or a gift offering, that payment takes effect on them.

messages.text: But if these birds are disqualified as sacrifices, let the prohibitions of payment to a prostitute and the price of a dog apply to consecrated animals, by the following a fortiori inference: If in the case of birds, which a blemish does not disqualify, the status of a prostitute’s payment and a dog’s price applies to them, then with regard to consecrated items, which a blemish does disqualify, is it not logical that the status of a prostitute’s payment and a dog’s price should apply to them?

notes.he: כדרבינן במתני' לכל נדר להביא את העוף:
notes.en: Payment and price take effect on them: as we include in the mishna, “for any vow,” to include the bird.

messages.text: Therefore, the verse states: “For any vow.” This serves to exclude those animals that have already been vowed to be sacrificed.

The only reason consecrated animals are disqualified is that the verse excludes them, through the word “vow.” But had the verse not excluded them, I would say that if one gives a prostitute sacrificial animals, or gives these animals in exchange for a dog, the prohibition of payment to a prostitute or a dog’s price applies to them. But this conclusion is problematic, as a consecrated animal is not his property, and there is an established principle that one cannot render an item prohibited if it does not belong to him. How then could one render it prohibited by giving it to a prostitute?

notes.dh: פרט לדבר הנדור כבר היינו מוקדשין שכבר נדורין הן
notes.he: הא אין אדם אוסר דבר שאינו שלו דשל הקדש הן והיכי חל אתננה עליהן:
notes.en: Excluding an item already vowed: that is, consecrated items, which are already vowed. But a person cannot forbid an item that is not his, for they belong to the Temple; so how would her payment take effect on them?

messages.text: This is referring to one who registers the prostitute for his Paschal offering (see Pesaḥim 61a), giving her a portion in it as payment for her services, and it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, who maintains that a Paschal offering is considered one’s personal property for the purposes of allowing additional people to register for it. As it is taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: a consecrated animal is not his property

notes.he: הא דאיצטריך קרא למעוטיה כגון שהפריש פסחו ולאחר זמן אמר לזונה הבעלי לי והימני על פסחי באתנניך וכיון דאמר רבי רשאי אדם למנות אחרים אם יצטרך למעות לשום דבר אלמא ממונו הוא ואימא ליחול עליה אתנן להכי איצטריך לכל נדר להוציא הנדור:
notes.en: To one who registers [her] for his Paschal offering: the case where the verse was needed to exclude it is, for example, where he set aside his Paschal offering and later said to a prostitute, “Be with me, and be registered on my Paschal offering as your payment.” And since Rabbi says a person may register others [on his Paschal offering] if he needs money for something, evidently it is his property, and one might say that payment takes effect on it. That is why “for any vow” was needed, to exclude what is vowed.

notes.dh: אמר ר' הושעיא בהני מוקדשין מיירי דישנן ברשותו
notes.he: כגון פסחו וממנה על פסחו באתננה ואליבא דר' היא דיכול לקנות מפסחו מה שצריך:
notes.en: Rav Hoshaya said: it speaks of consecrated items that are in his possession, such as his Paschal offering, where he registers her on his Paschal offering as her payment; and it is according to Rabbi, who holds that he may acquire from his Paschal offering what he needs.

messages.text: The verse states, with regard to the Paschal offering: “And if the household be too little for a lamb, then he and his neighbor next to his house shall take one” (Exodus 12:4). The phrase “if the household be too little” is interpreted to mean that the household cannot afford the basic necessities of the Festival.

verse.he: וְאִם־יִמְעַט הַבַּיִת מִהְיוֹת מִשֶּׂה וְלָקַח הוּא וּשְׁכֵנוֹ הַקָּרֹב אֶל־בֵּיתוֹ בְּמִכְסַת נְפָשֹׁת אִישׁ לְפִי אׇכְלוֹ תָּכֹסּוּ עַל־הַשֶּׂה׃
verse.en: But if the household is too small for a lamb, let it share one with a neighbor who dwells nearby, in proportion to the number of persons: you shall contribute for the lamb according to what each household will eat.

notes.he: דריש הכי שנתמעט ביתו שאין לו מה שהוא צריך [לקנות לצורך פסח דהיינו] מהיות משה החייהו משה שימנה אחרים עמו על פסחו ויתנו לו מעות:
notes.en: “And if the household be too little”: he expounds it thus: that his household became too little, that he does not have what he needs [to buy for the needs of the Paschal offering, that is,] “for a lamb [mihyot miseh]”: sustain him from the lamb, that he may register others with him on his Paschal offering and they give him money.

notes.dh: דתניא אם ימעט הבית מהיות משה
notes.he: כלומר אם נחסר לבית שאין לו מה שצריך לתקון הפסח כגון עצים או תבלין החייהו משה:
notes.en: As it is taught: “And if the household be too little for a lamb”: that is, if the household lacks, so that he does not have what he needs to prepare the Paschal offering, such as wood or spices, “sustain him from the lamb.”

messages.text: Based on this interpretation, the phrase “for a lamb [mihyot miseh]” is interpreted to mean: Sustain him from the lamb [haḥyeihu miseh], i.e., he may use the Paschal offering as a means of supporting himself. He takes money from his neighbor in return for registering that neighbor for a portion of his Paschal offering and uses the money to purchase his needs. This halakha applies only if one lacks sufficient means to purchase food to eat, but not if he lacks merely sufficient means to purchase other items.

notes.he: אם נתמעט הבית מכדי אכילה יקבל חיותו ומזונו מן השה שאין לו מה שיאכל החייהו משה אם אין לו עצים לצלותו מכדי אכילה הוא והחייהו ולא החייהו משה:
notes.en: From the needs of eating: if the household lacks the needs of eating, he may receive his sustenance and food from the lamb. If he has nothing to eat, “sustain him from the lamb”; if he has no wood to roast it, that too is “from the needs of eating,” and [the rule] “sustain him” [applies]. [The last words of the printed note, “and not sustain him from the lamb,” seem to belong to the next note.]

notes.he: שאם רוצה לעשות סחורה ונתמעט ביתו מכדי אותו מקח שאין לו מה ליתן בו אינו ממנה אחרים על פסחו בכך:
notes.en: And not from the needs of a purchase: if he wants to trade, and his household lacks the means for that purchase, so that he has nothing to pay for it, he does not register others on his Paschal offering for that.

notes.he: כלומר אם נחסר לו מצורך תקון אכילתו יכול ליקח מעות מאחרים וממנה על שם פסחו ויקח מעות ויקנה מהן עצים לצורך תקון אכילת פסחו ואל יקח מאותן מעות מקח אחר כגון טלית או כסות:
notes.en: From the needs of eating and not from the needs of a purchase: that is, if he lacks what he needs to prepare his meal, he may take money from others and register them on his Paschal offering, and buy wood with the money for preparing the eating of his Paschal offering; but he may not buy anything else with that money, such as a cloak or clothing.

messages.text: This lenient halakha applies even if one lacks sufficient means to purchase other necessary items, as, if he does not have sufficient funds he may register others with him for his Paschal offering and for his Festival peace offering. And his money that he receives for registering that person is non-sacred, as it is on this condition of registering others in exchange for the money which he receives from them that the Jewish people consecrate their Paschal offerings.

notes.dh: ר"א אף מכדי מקח שאם צריך לטלית או לדבר אחר ממנה אחרים כו'
notes.he: ומעות חולין ויעשה בהן צורכו שעל מנת כן הקדישו ישראל את פסחיהן שאם הוצרך לו דבר שימנה אחרים עמו ויתן המעות לצורכו. לטעמא דר' דאמר אף מכדי מקח אתנן חל עליו אי לאו דמעטי' קרא מנדר [דר' אליעזר סבר זה וזה גורם אסור אע"ג דהאי ולד בא מצד אחד של היתר של זכר [דאביו] של ולד אין בו איסור אפי' הכי כיון דיש באמו איסור זה וזה גורם להאי ולד ואסור ורבנן דמתניתין סברי זה וזה גורם מותר אבל עיברו כו':
notes.en:
Rabbi says: even from the needs of a purchase: that if he needs a cloak or something else, he registers others etc., and the money is non-sacred and he may use it for his needs, for it is on this condition that the Jewish people consecrated their Paschal offerings, that if he needs something he may register others with him and use the money for his needs. By the reasoning of Rabbi, who says even from the needs of a purchase, payment would take effect on it, had the verse not excluded it with “vow.”
[Rabbi Eliezer holds that when both this and that cause something, it is forbidden: even though this offspring comes from one permitted side, its father, which has no prohibition, nevertheless, since its mother is forbidden, both together cause this offspring, and it is forbidden. And the Rabbis of the mishna hold that when both this and that cause something, it is permitted. But if they became pregnant etc.]

messages.text: With regard to all animals whose sacrifice on the altar is prohibited, sacrifice of their offspring is permitted.
messages.quote: all animals whose sacrifice on the altar is prohibited

messages.text: This ruling that with regard to all animals whose sacrifice on the altar is prohibited, sacrifice of their offspring is permitted, is not unanimous but is the opinion of the Rabbis. And indeed it is taught with regard to this case:
And Rabbi Eliezer prohibits their offspring to be sacrificed on the altar.

This dispute applies in a case where the animals became pregnant and then were the objects of bestiality, thereby becoming prohibited to sacrifice on the altar. As Rabbi Eliezer holds that a fetus is considered the thigh of its mother and regarded as part of the animal, and is consequently prohibited like its mother. And the Rabbis hold that a fetus is not considered the thigh of its mother.

notes.he: והוא עצמו נרבע:
notes.en: A fetus is the thigh of its mother: and so it was itself the object of bestiality.

messages.text: But if the animals were the objects of bestiality and then became pregnant, everyone agrees that they are permitted.

notes.dh: אבל נרבעו ולבסוף עיברו ד"ה מותרין
notes.he: פירוש זה וזה גורם מותר וקשה דשמעינן ליה לר' אליעזר דאית ליה בפרק כל שעה (פסחים כז.) זה וזה גורם אסור וי"ל דהתם מיירי בדבר שאסור אף להדיוט והכא מיירי באיסור גבוה לבד [וע' תוס' סנהדרין פ: ד"ה אלא]:
notes.en: But if they were the object of bestiality and then became pregnant, all agree they are permitted: that is, [because] when both this and that cause something, it is permitted. This is difficult, for we find that Rabbi Eliezer holds in chapter Kol Sha’ah (Pesaḥim 27a) that when both this and that cause something, it is forbidden. One may answer that there it deals with an item forbidden even to an ordinary person, and here it deals with a prohibition for the altar alone. [See Tosafot Sanhedrin 80b, beginning “ela.”]

messages.text: This dispute applies in a case where the animals were the objects of bestiality and then became pregnant, as Rabbi Eliezer holds that when both this permitted factor and that prohibited factor cause a certain situation, the resulting item is prohibited. Since the mother of this offspring is prohibited, the offspring is likewise prohibited, despite the fact that its father is permitted. And the Rabbis hold that when this permitted factor and that prohibited factor cause a result, it, i.e., the offspring, is permitted like its father.

notes.he: הזכר שבא על בהמה זו והיא גרמו לולד שיבא והרי גרמוהו איסור והיתר דאביו מותר ואמו אסורה:
notes.en: Both this and that cause: the male that mated with this animal, and it [the mother], caused the offspring to come about, so a prohibition and a permission caused it, for its father is permitted and its mother forbidden.

messages.text: But in a case where the animals became pregnant and then were the object of bestiality, everyone agrees that they are prohibited.
And Rava conforms to his standard line of reasoning in this regard, as Rava said:
messages.quote: The offspring of a female animal that was the object of bestiality when it was pregnant is prohibited

messages.text: The offspring of a female animal that was the object of bestiality when it was pregnant is prohibited to be sacrificed on the altar, as it is considered as though it, the mother, and its offspring were both the object of bestiality. Likewise, the offspring of a pregnant cow that gores and kills a person is prohibited, because it is as though it, the mother, and its offspring both gored.
Some state another version of the previous discussion:

This dispute applies in a case where the animals were the object of bestiality when they already had the status of sacrificial animals. As Rabbi Eliezer holds that the offspring are also prohibited to be sacrificed on the altar, as their sacrifice is considered a degradation of consecrated items, and degradation of consecrated items is significant. And the Rabbis hold that the offspring may be sacrificed, as they maintain that this is not considered a degradation of consecrated items.

notes.he: ל"א מחלוקת שנרבעו כשהן מוקדשין אע"ג דבתר הכי עיברו ר' אלעזר סבר אמרינן [ביזוי] (בהא) מילתא למיקרב וולדותיהן הואיל ונרבעו כשהן מוקדשין אבל נרבעו כשהן חולין ואחר עיבורו הואיל ונשתנו שהקדישן דברי הכל מותרין:
notes.en: Another version: the dispute is where they were the object of bestiality when they were consecrated, even though they became pregnant afterwards. Rabbi Elazar [so Rabbeinu Gershom’s text, for Rabbi Eliezer] holds that we say it is a degradation to offer their offspring, since they were the object of bestiality when consecrated. But if they were the object of bestiality when they were non-sacred, and after that he consecrated them, since they changed, all agree they are permitted. [The printed note then repeats itself: their pregnancy, since they changed when he consecrated them, all agree they are permitted.]

messages.text: But in a case where the animals were the object of bestiality when they were non-sacred, and were subsequently consecrated, since their status was changed by their consecration, everyone agrees that they are permitted.

This dispute applies in a case where the animals were the object of bestiality when they were non-sacred, as Rabbi Eliezer holds that even the sacrifice of this offspring is considered degrading to sacrificial animals, and degradation of sacrificial animals is significant, and therefore they are prohibited. And the Rabbis hold that since their status was changed by their consecration, they are permitted.

notes.he: ולמאן דאמר בשחיטת חולין טריפה אינה יולדת. שאין מתעברת משכחת לה האי ולד טריפה דקתני כגון שעיברה ואח"כ נטרפה:
notes.en: And Rava said that Rav Naḥman said etc. And according to the one who says in Sheḥitat Ḥullin that a tereifa does not give birth, that is, does not become pregnant, you find this case of the offspring of a tereifa that is taught [in the mishna] where it became pregnant and afterwards became a tereifa.

messages.text: But in a case where the animals were the object of bestiality when they already had the status of sacrificial animals, everyone agrees that they are prohibited.

messages.caption: Where Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis disagree about the offspring, in both versions of Rav Naḥman and Rava.

messages.text: Continues on 31a: the mishna’s dispute over the offspring of a tereifa, and whether a tereifa can give birth.
